# Grammatical categories

Each item tests one grammatical structure (negation, reversible passive,
relative clause and so on); the child hears a sentence and picks the
picture that matches it.

```{r trog-cats}
trog_items <- items |>
  mutate(category = coalesce(na_if(item_group_label, ""), item_group))
trog_cats <- trog_items |>
  group_by(category) |>
  summarise(n_items = n(), difficulty = mean(difficulty), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(difficulty)
```

```{r trog-cat-plot, fig.height=7}
#| label: fig-trog-categories
#| fig-cap: "Calibrated item difficulty by grammatical category: each item (points) and the category mean (bar)."
trog_items |>
  mutate(category = factor(category, trog_cats$category)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = difficulty, y = category)) +
  geom_point(colour = "#4477AA", alpha = 0.6) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(x = "Item difficulty", y = NULL)
```

The easiest categories are
`r paste(head(trog_cats$category, 3), collapse = ", ")`; the hardest are
`r paste(rev(tail(trog_cats$category, 3)), collapse = ", ")`.
`r sum(trog_cats$n_items == 1)` of the `r nrow(trog_cats)` categories have a
single item, so their means are one item's difficulty.
